text:
rory_ae: Urgent: Orion POC load run is returning a stream of 5xxs while ramping. Theyre blasting 90-180rps in short bursts. Customer demo in 20m. Need a quick mitigation and a one-line explanation for the AE to share.

dylan_support: Can you paste a sample error and the region/model? Any request_id?

rory_ae: region=us-gov-west, model=rw-open-3b-q4-hosted. Sample from their harness: 
```
POST /v1/complete
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-rw-queue-depth: 58
x-rw-backpressure: true
{"error":"upstream overloaded","request_id":"req_orion_55"}
```
Also some 504s.

priya_infra: Queue saturation + autoscaler lag. Two fast paths: 1) API-key scoped soft-failover to the 1B variant, 2) temporarily attach the customer to burstpool/warm-replica if policy allows. Quick note: our burstpool coldstart is ~35s in gov regions.

dylan_support: Is there an API-only toggle we can flip quickly so we don't touch infra?

priya_infra: Yes. Command I can run now (no infra spins): 
```
redwoodctl api-keys set --key id=key-orion --failover-model=rw-open-1b-q4 --failover-threshold-ms=550
```
That routes requests above 550ms to the smaller model. Keeps most traffic on 3B and avoids autoscale spin.

zack_se: If AE asks about pricing delta for a short demo if we instead provision a warm replica (min_replicas=1), what's a quick estimate for gov region? Need a figure to tell customer.

priya_infra: GOV pricing is higher. Rough ballpark: min_replicas=1 for rw-open-3b-q4 in us-gov-west ~$1200/day. For a one-hour demo that's ~+$50. Soft-failover cost is negligible for short bursts. I'll follow up with exact quote.

alert-bot: Alert A-2951-11: pool rw-open-3b-q4 (us-gov-west) queue_depth peaked at 62.

dylan_support: While failover rolls, grab logs for req_orion_55 and the queue/memory series: `curl -H "x-request-id: req_orion_55" https://logs.internal/bundle` and `redwoodctl metrics get --name queue_depth --since 20m --filter customer=orion`. Also check pending_coldstarts.

rory_ae: I uploaded the log bundle to INC-2026-2951-03 and notified the customer the team is applying a temporary soft-failover. They asked whether routing to 1B changes model fidelity. AE wants a one-liner: what to tell them?

zack_se: Say: "Were enabling an automated latency-based fallback to a smaller model during brief spikes to keep the demo fluid; core functionality is preserved but some edge-case generation quality may vary." Keep it brief.

priya_infra: I flipped the failover flag for key-orion. Rolling now. Also toggled a short client-side guidance: recommend ramping at 40rps per 30s or using a token-bucket to avoid bursty fan-out.

dylan_support: After the flip, error counts dropped by ~80% in the next 2 minutes. Leaving incident open for infra follow-ups: audit trial routing policy, consider adding a "prewarm" API for scheduled demos, and review burstpool attach thresholds (queue_depth > 50 vs > 40 mismatch).

rory_ae: Customer confirmed demo completed and appreciated the quick note. AE asks for a short FAQ entry about demo best-practices and estimated cost for prewarm. Can someone draft that?

zack_se: I'll draft a one-paragraph FAQ and include the cost bullets.

priya_infra: Follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-2951-03: 
- Investigate why burstpool didn't attach automatically (policy gate vs metric emission)
- Add a lightweight scheduled prewarm API for booked demos (prebind 1 replica)
- Consider lowering coldstart to <30s for top-5 models in gov regions

dylan_support: Thanks all. Demo saved. Leaving thread open for the infra tickets. :thumbsup:
